**The order.**

1. **Simulation fixes and default sleep** (built). Finish Parts G, E and H, the benchmarks and the report, as in `docs/ROUND-PROMPT.md` and `docs/ROUND-PROMPT-ADDITIONS.md`. Merge into `develop`, which this item creates.
2. **The visual overhaul.** Specification: `docs/prompts/VISUAL-OVERHAUL.md`, which Haakon placed in the main checkout (if it is still untracked there, copy it into the item's branch and commit it first), and "The map (built in item 2)" under Spectator mode, including the date labels and the "follow this character" view. Presentation only. Years are counted from 1345 BCE ("Calendar" in the Ideas tab); item 6 moves the first year to 1346 BCE. Its first milestone, before anything else: a whole game can be watched on a phone. Phone play comes after.
3. **Small record items.** "Tablets are objects in a place" (archives at the capital; spies can copy from them; whoever takes a capital gains copies of its archive), "Swapped tablets" (an envoy replacing an inventory tablet with a forgery stating less, under the existing forgery rules) and "The richest characters" (a ranking by wealth at the end of a game; if characters' gold is not tracked yet, track what they gain and spend). All in the Ideas tab.
4. **Second agent simulation, with model characters.** First, three fixes, each with its own commit and tests, the first two left by item 2's report. (a) A leak: the engine's seat view lists a foreign spy posted at a court together with its employer. A king must see a foreign spy at his court, and who employs it, only once his court has caught it or otherwise learned it; add the case to the hidden-state tests. Agents would exploit the leak, so it is fixed before the simulation. (b) Phone performance, because watching on a phone is the first milestone: playing a season must not freeze the page (it blocks for up to about 3 s on a slow emulated phone, with the script kings' look-ahead on the single WebAssembly thread), and the first load must be much faster than about 20 s on slow 4G. Use the fixes the report names, such as running the engine in a Web Worker, ahead-of-time compilation, and splitting the SDK path out of Amarna.Llm, keeping seeds and replays exact; measure before and after on the same throttled profile. (c) A latent bug: a \`?? Power.Egypt\` fallback makes Egypt the court of a character with no employer or location; a character with neither belongs to no court. Then the simulation: extend the `sim/` kit so envoys and spies are agents too, isolated like the kings, and run seed 7 and one new seed for ten seasons with sleep as the default. Measure what the first simulation could not: whether model envoys lie, skim and cover up, and how they compare with script envoys of the same traits; how often kings reopen their orders after an audience; wake-ups and call sizes under the new triggers. **Stop for review:** the results show whether model characters are too honest, in which case they are given real stakes, never engine-rolled decisions or priming to misbehave ("Stakes, not dispositions" in the Ideas tab), and whether the message-kind fallback for reopening is needed. Before stopping, make the kit playable for Haakon: "Local play on a Claude subscription", a human seat in the locally running game against file-seat kings answered by guarded, isolated king agents, so that at this review he can start playing model kings himself.
5. **The siege package (pillar 8).** Walls that vary and can be strengthened, storming and besieging, envoys leaving a besieged city, terrain per province and per connection, deserts costing supplies, islands protected by the sea, and slow absorption of conquered land. A kingdom falls with its capital, its land passing to the conqueror ("A kingdom falls with its capital" in this tab); it comes in this package, since without walls a capital can fall in the third season. With it, "A fallen player's game is over": the fallen player watches the rest in god view, a setting on by default that a table can turn off, in which case he watches with what his kingdom knew when it fell. Specification: "Tempo of war" and "Walls and terrain" in this tab, and question 5 of the old round report, with its terrain lists. Retire the temporary trigger for troops next to the capital. The desert cost follows "Different data, same rules": question 5 exempts Egypt's armies in Sinai, after the Ways of Horus; build it instead as "an army in its own land pays no desert cost", so Egypt is exempt because it holds Sinai, and so is anyone who takes it. Set first guesses aiming at about 5–10 seasons from the first hostile entry to a capital's fall, with capitals still falling in most games; tuning waits for item 18. Military timings start from the pace of letters and what is realistic for the period, and item 18 tunes them ("Distance-based marching" in the Ideas tab). **Stop for review:** a first look at how long wars and games now run; game length and the ending rule are set in item 18.
